result.title: Verifying Agents in Rubric-Graded Environments
result.summary: As AI agents take on increasingly open-ended and complex tasks, verifying their outputs has proven to be difficult. Rubric-graded agent environments, where a verifier judges multiple natural-language criteria against the deliverables and environment state changes produced by the agent, have emerged as a popular paradigm. We conduct the first systematic study of verifiers for rubric-graded agent environments. First, we create BankerVerifierBench (BVB), a meta-evaluation dataset of 2,464 human-judged rubric criteria across 24 investment-banking tasks. Next, we develop a methodology that derives from any rubric corpus the capabilities a verifier should possess, yielding a nine-capability taxonomy that we distill into three general design principles---reactive verification, environment alignment, and domain guidance---which we implement in Gandalf, an open-source verifier. Finally, we evaluate Gandalf against three existing verifiers on BVB. Gandalf matches or exceeds every baseline's F1 at lower cost: with Gemini 3 Flash it matches the strongest baseline's F1 (0.864 vs. 0.852) at one-fifth of its cost, and with GPT-5.4 models it improves F1 by over 0.12 at lower cost. Gandalf also generalizes to OpenClaw, a structurally different personal-productivity environment, where it again achieves the highest F1 (0.955 vs. 0.934 for the best baseline). We release BVB, Gandalf, and the code and data to reproduce our experiments.

AI.brief_summary: 论文系统研究「rubric 评分」型 agent 环境的验证器：构建含 2,464 条人工判定评分标准的投资银行任务基准 BVB，归纳出九类验证能力与三项设计原则，并实现开源验证器 Gandalf，在多个基线与另一类环境上以更低成本取得相当或更高 F1。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「反应式验证」「与环境状态对齐」的多准则核验方法，可能可供核查如何判断 VLM 推理产出是否真正依据视觉证据、以及为推理轨迹构造 rubric 式监督与评价信号。
